title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: S&P 500 +0.9%, Nasdaq +1%, Dow +509 pts Friday, snapping a 4-day losing streak as oil and Treasury yields paused their surge.
Markets: Traders now price ~87% odds of a Fed rate HIKE at next week's Sept 15-16 meeting (up from 72%) after hot inflation data; the 10-yr yield sits near 4.97%.
Macro: August CPI rose 3.4% Y/Y (in line with July), but core CPI +0.3% M/M topped forecasts, reinforcing sticky inflation.
Macro: University of Michigan consumer sentiment sank to 47.8 in September (from 51.7) on rising fuel costs and trade tensions.

Macro/Policy: Houthi forces seized the Bab al-Mandeb strait chokepoint plus Mocha port and Perim Island; Saudi Arabia shut its East-West pipeline after drone strikes, putting both major Saudi export routes under threat.
Macro/Policy: Brent crude spiked toward $108 before easing to ~$104-105/barrel; U.S. diesel hit a record $6/gallon, up 60% Y/Y, feeding into broader transport and consumer costs.
Companies: Dell shares jumped 12% after a bullish RBC initiation citing AI infrastructure and agentic-workload demand.
Companies: GE Aerospace agreed to buy castings maker Consolidated Precision Products for $11.75B ($7B cash plus debt) to meet rising aerospace/defense demand.
Companies: PayPal's new CEO Enrique Lores is planning to go it alone rather than sell the company, aiming to turn Venmo into a full money-management app.
Ahead: Fed decision and August retail sales data both due next week.
